# Spotto AWS purpose-scoped role

Role purposes: resource-discovery, commitments-planning, billing-definition
Role name: SpottoReadOnlyRole
External ID: spotto-0f1e2d3c-4b5a-6978-8796-a5b4c3d2e1f0

## Trust policy
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowSpottoCloudEngineAccess",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::999900001111:role/SpottoEngine"
      },
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {
          "sts:ExternalId": "spotto-0f1e2d3c-4b5a-6978-8796-a5b4c3d2e1f0"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Discovery permissions
SpottoGuardrails includes the engine-owned inventory and security action allowlist, version 2026-10-16.1.
For existing roles, attach this generated replacement and verify collection, then detach ReadOnlyAccess and SecurityAudit. Keeping those managed policies attached retains their broader permissions.

## Security posture and findings
The discovery policy includes the exact read operations used for Security Hub CSPM, GuardDuty and Inspector. Service control policies, permission boundaries or explicit denies can still cause access denied.
For a security percentage, enable Security Hub CSPM with a security standard and AWS Config recording in the Regions included in your Spotto account scope. GuardDuty and Inspector findings are collected independently when those services are enabled.
Spotto reads security evidence; it does not enable security services or change findings. A disabled service or denied read is shown as unavailable, not as a zero or a healthy score.
Security setup and exact read permissions: https://docs.spotto.ai/portal/cloud-account-aws/security
